claim: In multi-agent reinforcement learning for autonomous vehicle lane-changing in mixed traffic, a local reward design yields larger evaluation rewards and smaller variance compared to a global reward design, and this performance advantage increases with the number of vehicles.
falsifier: In a multi-agent RL lane-changing simulator with mixed traffic, compare training curves of agents using local rewards versus global rewards under varying vehicle densities; measure average reward and variance across episodes.

conditions: multi-agent advantage actor-critic (MA2C) framework with parameter sharing
mixed traffic with human-driven vehicles (HDVs) and autonomous vehicles (AVs)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task (lane-changing), traffic modes, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Local reward design versus for larger evaluation rewards

claim: The post-training loss of a pruned large language model can be predicted by a scaling law that depends on the model size before pruning, the number of post-training tokens, the pruning rate, and the loss before pruning, as formalized by a mathematical equation.
falsifier: The scaling law can be tested by fitting the equation to post-training loss data from pruned LLMs with varying pre-pruning sizes, post-training tokens, pruning rates, and pre-pruning losses, and evaluating prediction accuracy.

conditions: the law is derived from theoretical considerations and validated on Llama-3 series models with depth pruning at approximately 15% pruning rate
the law generalizes to larger dataset sizes, larger model sizes, and higher pruning rates
exclusions: evidence is limited to the reported system (Llama-3 series, depth pruning) and experimental conditions; transfer beyond these is unestablished

title: Pruned large language models–post-training loss theorem
